title: Driveway Sealer Home Depot: Which of 5 Picks Fits Your Drive
metaDescription: For blacktop, the Home Depot driveway sealer to pick is a filler sealer like Latex-ite Airport Grade; a 600 sq ft drive takes 4 to 5 pails for two coats.
h1: Driveway Sealer at Home Depot: Which One Should You Buy?
keywords: home depot concrete sealer for driveways
black top crack filler home depot
intro:
The driveway sealer to buy at Home Depot depends first on your surface: for blacktop, a polymer-modified filler sealer such as Latex-ite Airport Grade suits most driveways, and a typical 600 square foot two-car drive takes four or five pails for two coats. For concrete, a penetrating silane-siloxane such as Foundation Armor SX5000 is the low-maintenance choice, and an acrylic like BEHR Premium Wet-Look is the pick when you want shine.

The seasonal aisle mixes asphalt pails, concrete sealers and repair products on neighboring pallets, and grabbing the wrong one is the costliest mistake shoppers make there. This guide does not quote prices or promise what your store has in stock, since both vary by location and season. It shows you which type of product to put in the cart, how to read the labels, how many pails you need, and how to plan the job so the coat lasts.
quickAnswer: Asphalt in fair shape: a filler sealer such as Latex-ite Airport Grade. Rough, gray, long-unsealed asphalt: a heavy premium pail such as Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000. Price-first blacktop refresh: Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop Filler and Sealer. Plain concrete: Foundation Armor SX5000 penetrating sealer. Stamped or colored concrete: BEHR Premium Wet-Look. Check homedepot.com for local stock before you go, and buy crack filler on the same trip.

sections.heading: Driveway Sealer at Home Depot: The Short Answer
sections.body:
| Your driveway | Product type | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blacktop, fading but sound | Polymer-modified filler sealer | Latex-ite Airport Grade |
| Blacktop, rough and long unsealed | Premium heavy-solids emulsion | Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 |
| Blacktop, fair, budget first | Value filler sealer | Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop |
| Plain concrete | Silane-siloxane penetrating sealer | Foundation Armor SX5000 |
| Stamped or colored concrete | Acrylic wet-look sealer | BEHR Premium Wet-Look |

Start with the surface, then the condition, then the brand. Black asphalt sealer on concrete peels; a concrete sealer on asphalt does almost nothing. Within each surface, the condition of the driveway decides the tier, not your budget.

Availability differs between stores and through the season, and some of these, especially concrete penetrants, are more often sold online. Use the product types above if your store carries a different brand.

sections.heading: Which Driveway Sealer Should You Buy at Home Depot?
sections.body:
These picks come from manufacturer labels and data sheets, coverage and cure specs, the job each formula is built for, and recurring themes in owner feedback.

### Best overall for asphalt: Latex-ite Airport Grade

The middle-of-the-shelf pail that suits most blacktop. It is a polymer-modified filler sealer, so it carries fine mineral solids that settle into worn texture and hairline cracks as you squeegee. That gives a thicker film and a richer black than budget sealcoats. The label lists resistance to gasoline and motor oil, useful on the garage apron. Plan on fewer square feet per pail than a thin sealer and budget two coats. Our [Latex-ite review](/latex-ite-driveway-sealer-review/) goes deeper.

### Best premium for asphalt: Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000

The top of Gardner-Gibson's Black Jack line: heavily filled and polymer-modified, for owners who would rather spend more once than recoat every other spring. The heavy film fills open, gray texture better than lighter pails. On a smooth driveway sealed two years ago it is overkill. It spreads slowly, so plan smaller sections or a helper on big driveways.

### Best value for asphalt: Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop Filler and Sealer

An asphalt filler sealer, not an epoxy, despite the name it shares with Rust-Oleum's garage floor kits. It carries enough filler to even out moderate wear and gives a clean black for the first season. The film is lighter than premium pails, so recoat closer to every two years on a busy drive.

### Best for plain concrete: Foundation Armor SX5000

A silane-siloxane penetrating sealer. It soaks in and lines the pores with a water repellent, so water and dissolved salt bead and run off instead of driving freeze-thaw scaling. There is no film to peel, wear in tire paths or turn slick, and the concrete keeps its natural look. It does not add gloss and resists surface stains less than a film. It is commonly an online or ship-to-store item, so order ahead.

### Best for a glossy concrete finish: BEHR Premium Wet-Look Sealer

An acrylic film-former that darkens the concrete and adds a wet-look sheen, striking on stamped, colored or exposed-aggregate driveways. The film also helps oil and dirt clean up. The trade-off is upkeep: acrylics wear in tire paths, can whiten if moisture is trapped, and usually need a fresh coat every couple of years. Add an anti-slip grit where the drive slopes.

sections.heading: Is Your Driveway Asphalt or Concrete?
sections.body:
It sounds obvious, but older, patched or dirty driveways fool people.

### Signs of asphalt

Black or faded gray, slightly soft on a hot afternoon, no straight control joints, and edges that crumble into the lawn. Asphalt needs an asphalt emulsion or filler sealer, which replaces the binder sun and oxygen strip away, slows water intrusion and restores color.

### Signs of concrete

Light gray, hard in any weather, poured in slabs with straight joints cut or tooled every several feet. Concrete needs a penetrating repellent or a clear film sealer. Put black sealer on it and it never bonds properly and peels in sheets.

### Two-in-one products

Some products are sold for both surfaces. They can work as a light protective coat but rarely do either job as well as a dedicated product. If you have both, such as an asphalt driveway with a concrete apron, buy two products.

### Pavers

Interlocking pavers are a third case. They need a paver sealer that also stabilizes the joint sand. Our [paver sealer guide](/best-paver-sealer/) covers those.

sections.heading: Budget, Mid-Range or Premium: Which Tier Does Your Driveway Need?
sections.body:
Every brand sells about three tiers, and the condition of the asphalt picks the tier, not how much you want to spend. A premium pail on smooth, young asphalt pays for solids with nothing to fill. The cheapest pail on a gray, open driveway soaks in and vanishes, and you lose the weekend.

### Read the surface in bright sun

- **Dark, smooth and tight, a little faded:** a budget or mid-range emulsion. One careful coat may be enough.
- **Gray, stones showing, water darkens it instead of beading:** it has lost binder. Use a filler sealer in two coats.
- **Rough, porous and unsealed for years:** a premium heavy-solids pail, two coats, and patience on the spread.

### Climate

Where winters bring hard freezes and road salt, polymer modification is worth paying for, because a brittle film cracks with the pavement. Where freeze-thaw is rare, UV is the main enemy, and a mid-range filler sealer on schedule does the job for less.

### Cost per year, not per pail

A premium coat that lasts three years can beat a budget coat redone yearly once you count your weekends and the tools. That only holds if you do the prep; a premium pail over dust and oil fails just as fast. Our guide on [how often to seal your driveway](/how-often-should-you-seal-your-driveway/) helps set a realistic schedule, and [oil-based vs water-based sealer](/oil-based-vs-water-based-driveway-sealer/) explains the chemistry question that sometimes comes up in this aisle.

sections.heading: What Do the Words on a Driveway Sealer Pail Mean?
sections.body:
Driveway pails use a small vocabulary. Knowing it saves money.

| Label term | What it means | Who it suits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sealer / sealcoat | Thin asphalt emulsion | Young, smooth driveways on a regular refresh |
| Filler sealer | Emulsion plus mineral filler | Weathered, gray, slightly porous asphalt |
| Polymer-modified / rubberized | Added polymers for flexibility | Cold climates and longer recoat cycles |
| Coal-tar-free | Asphalt-based binder | Everyone; required in some states |
| Penetrating (concrete) | Silane or siloxane repellent | Concrete in salt and freeze-thaw areas |
| Wet look (concrete) | Acrylic surface film | Decorative or stamped concrete |

### Service-life claims

Years printed on the front of a pail are the maker's figure for ideal application. Use them to rank pails within one brand's line, not to predict your driveway. Heavy traffic, shade and skipped prep shorten every one of them.

### The side panel matters most

Minimum temperature, rain-free hours and time before driving are the conditions under which the coverage and lifespan on the front were reached. Treat them as requirements. Our guides to [what temperature to seal a driveway](/what-temperature-to-seal-driveway/) and [how long driveway sealer takes to dry](/how-long-for-driveway-sealer-to-dry/) explain why.

sections.heading: How Many Pails of Driveway Sealer Should You Buy?
sections.body:
Measure the paved area, length times width, and add the apron and any parking pad. Divide by the label's single-coat coverage, then double for two coats. Most blacktop filler sealers in 4.75-gallon pails list somewhere around 250 to 400 square feet per pail; thin emulsions cover more, heavy premium pails less.

| Driveway | Approx. area | Filler sealer, 2 coats | Thin emulsion, 2 coats |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Single car, short | 300 sq ft | 2 to 3 pails | 2 pails |
| Two car, standard | 600 sq ft | 4 to 5 pails | 3 to 4 pails |
| Two car, long | 1,000 sq ft | 6 to 8 pails | 5 to 6 pails |
| Three car with turnaround | 1,500 sq ft | 9 to 12 pails | 7 to 9 pails |

### Low end or high end?

Use the low end of the label range for older, rough asphalt that drinks the first coat, and the high end for smooth surfaces sealed in the last few years. Then add one spare pail. Unopened pails are generally returnable within the store's return window, and the spare saves a store run with half the driveway wet.

### Weight

A full pail weighs roughly 50 to 60 pounds. Six pails is the better part of 350 pounds, so use a flatbed cart, check your vehicle's payload, and consider pickup or delivery for a big order.

### Price

Pail prices move with the season and promotions, so check homedepot.com for current figures. For a full materials-versus-contractor comparison, see [how much it costs to seal a driveway](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/).

sections.heading: What Else Should You Buy With Driveway Sealer?
sections.body:
The sealer is half the purchase. The tools and prep products decide whether it lasts.

### Application tools

- A squeegee or long-handled sealer brush.
- A stiff push broom and a trim brush for edges.
- A drill-mounted mixing paddle; filler settles hard in the pail.
- Painter's tape or plastic sheeting for the garage floor and walks.
- Disposable gloves, old shoes and rags. Dried sealer does not come out of clothes.

### Prep products

- A driveway cleaner or degreaser; see our [driveway cleaner](/best-driveway-cleaner/) picks.
- An oil-spot primer for stains that stay tacky after scrubbing. Our guide to [removing oil stains from a driveway](/how-to-remove-oil-stains-from-driveway/) covers the cleaning.
- Crack filler sized to your cracks: pourable for narrow cracks, rope filler for medium ones, a trowel patch or cold patch for wide cracks and holes. Our [driveway crack filler rankings](/best-driveway-crack-filler/) compare them.

### Washing

If the driveway needs a pressure wash, a surface cleaner attachment gives a far more even result than a wand; our [surface cleaner](/best-surface-cleaner-for-pressure-washer/) guide lists models that fit common washers.

sections.heading: Should You Buy In-Store, Online or for Pickup?
sections.body:
### Check stock before you drive

Product pages show availability at your local store, and sealer goes quickly on the first warm weekends of spring. If the store shows only a few pails, order online for in-store pickup so they are held for you.

### Order specialty items early

Concrete penetrating sealers and some premium products are more often sold online and shipped to the store or the house. Order them about a week before your planned weekend.

### Big orders

A large pail order may be worth having delivered. Compare the delivery fee with the time and fuel of hauling a few hundred pounds yourself.

### Timing the purchase

The aisle fills in early spring and thins out in fall. The widest choice, including premium pails, is usually in April and May. If you plan to seal in September, buy in August rather than counting on fall leftovers. Store pails indoors, off the floor, and never let them freeze; a frozen emulsion separates and is ruined. Do not stockpile across years, because settled filler in an old pail can be very hard to remix.

### Returns

Keep the receipt and leave spare pails sealed. Return terms can change, so check the current policy, but an unopened pail is usually the easiest thing in this aisle to bring back.

sections.heading: How Do You Plan Sealing Day So the Coat Lasts?
sections.body:
Treat it as a two-day job.

### Day one: prep

1. Trim grass back from the edges, then sweep and blow the surface clean.
2. Scrub oil spots and prime any that stay tacky.
3. Wash with cleaner or pressure wash.
4. Fill cracks and patch holes, following those products' cure times.
5. Let everything dry through the rest of the day and overnight.

### Day two: seal

1. Start mid-morning once the dew is gone and the pavement is warm, at about 50 degrees F or more and rising.
2. Tape the garage threshold, cut in the edges with a brush, then pour and squeegee in sections from the garage toward the street so you never trap yourself.
3. Let the first coat firm up, often a few hours in sun, then apply the second in the opposite direction.
4. Block the driveway. Keep cars off for at least a full day, preferably two, and longer when nights are cool or the air is muggy.

### Two thin coats, never one thick one

A thick single coat skins over, stays soft underneath, and cracks or tracks. Two thin coats use the same product and cure harder.

### Weather

Check the hourly forecast that morning. If a shower surprises you, see [rain after driveway sealing](/rain-after-driveway-sealing/). For full technique, read [how to seal a driveway](/how-to-seal-a-driveway/), and for the seasonal window, the [best time to seal a driveway](/best-time-to-seal-driveway/). Concrete owners should follow [how to seal a concrete driveway](/how-to-seal-a-concrete-driveway/) instead.

sections.heading: When Will No Sealer From the Aisle Help?
sections.body:
Sealer protects good pavement. It does not repair bad pavement.

### Failing asphalt

Widespread alligator cracking, sunken areas, potholes and crumbling edges mean the base underneath has failed. A coat of sealer looks good for a few weeks before the same cracks return. Our page on [sealing asphalt pros and cons](/sealing-asphalt-driveway-pros-and-cons/) helps you decide whether sealing is still worth it.

### New asphalt

Fresh blacktop needs months to cure. Sealing too soon can trap oils and leave the surface soft. Our guide on [when to seal a new asphalt driveway](/when-should-you-seal-a-new-asphalt-driveway/) gives the timeline.

### Damaged concrete

Sealer will not stop structural cracks, lift heaved slabs or reverse scaling that has already happened. It slows further damage. If the surface is flaking badly, talk to a concrete contractor about resurfacing first.

For everything else, the right pail and a careful weekend give real value. Our [asphalt driveway sealer rankings](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/) cover brands beyond this aisle, and the [Menards driveway sealer](/driveway-sealer-menards/) guide covers the Midwest chain.

mistakes.title: Grabbing an asphalt pail for a concrete driveway
mistakes.body: Black emulsion sealers are made for asphalt only. On concrete they never bond and peel within a season, leaving a patchy black mess that is harder to remove than it was to apply. Confirm your surface before you shop and use a penetrating or acrylic sealer on concrete.

mistakes.title: Buying exactly the calculated pail count
mistakes.body: Rough asphalt drinks more than the label average, and running out mid-coat leaves a visible lap line and a wet driveway while you drive back to the store. Buy one spare pail and return it unopened if you do not need it.

mistakes.title: Leaving pails in a hot truck or a cold garage
mistakes.body: Emulsion sealers are ruined if they freeze, and a pail baking in a truck bed can skin over at the top. Store pails indoors at moderate temperatures, off the concrete floor, and use them in the season you bought them.

mistakes.title: Skipping the oil-spot primer
mistakes.body: Emulsion will not bond to oil-soaked asphalt, so a stain that stays tacky after scrubbing becomes a bald patch within weeks. A small can of primer costs little next to the pails, and it is the difference between an even finish and a spotty one.

mistakes.title: Trusting the first warm weekend of spring
mistakes.body: The first warm Saturday brings everyone to the aisle, but nights may still drop below 50 degrees, which stalls curing. Wait for a stretch where days and nights both stay mild, and check the hourly forecast for rain the morning you start.

faqs.q: What is the best driveway sealer at Home Depot?
faqs.a: For most asphalt driveways, a polymer-modified filler sealer such as Latex-ite Airport Grade. For rough, long-unsealed blacktop, Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 builds a heavier film. For concrete, a penetrating silane-siloxane such as Foundation Armor SX5000 is the low-maintenance choice, and BEHR Premium Wet-Look suits stamped concrete. Check homedepot.com for local stock.

faqs.q: How many 5-gallon pails of asphalt sealer do I need?
faqs.a: Divide your driveway area by the label coverage, then double it for two coats. Filler sealers in 4.75-gallon pails typically list about 250 to 400 square feet per pail per coat, so a 600 square foot driveway needs about four or five pails. Use the low end for rough asphalt and buy one spare pail to return unopened.

faqs.q: What concrete driveway sealer should I buy at Home Depot?
faqs.a: For plain broom-finished concrete, a penetrating silane-siloxane such as Foundation Armor SX5000 protects against water and salt with no film to peel. For stamped or colored concrete where you want gloss, an acrylic like BEHR Premium Wet-Look. Never use black asphalt sealer on concrete, and let new concrete cure about 28 days first.

faqs.q: What blacktop crack filler should I get at Home Depot?
faqs.a: Match it to the crack. For narrow cracks, a pourable rubberized asphalt filler is quickest. For cracks of about 1/8 to 1/2 inch, a rope filler melted with a torch gives a tougher, more flexible seal. Wider cracks need backer rod or a trowel patch, and holes need cold patch. Let filler cure before sealing over it.

faqs.q: Is Home Depot driveway sealer as good as professional sealcoating?
faqs.a: A premium retail pail applied in two thin coats on a clean, crack-filled driveway can perform close to a pro job. Crews spray bulk emulsion with sand and additives and work faster on large areas. On short driveways, DIY usually costs far less. On very long ones, a reputable crew's quote can come close to the cost of the pails alone.

faqs.q: When is the best time to buy driveway sealer at Home Depot?
faqs.a: Buy close to the weekend you will seal, ideally in spring or early summer when the aisle is fullest and premium pails are easiest to find. If you plan to seal in fall, buy in late summer. Do not store pails over winter in an unheated space, because a frozen emulsion separates and is ruined.

faqs.q: How long should I keep cars off a freshly sealed driveway?
faqs.a: At least 24 hours, and 48 hours is safer, longer when nights are cool or the air is humid. Foot traffic is usually fine after several hours in warm sun. Turning the steering wheel while parked on a fresh coat scuffs it fastest, so block the entrance with tape or a sawhorse until it is firm.

bottomLine: At Home Depot, buy for the surface first and the condition second. Blacktop that is fading but sound gets a filler sealer such as Latex-ite Airport Grade; rough, neglected blacktop justifies Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000; a fair driveway on a two-year cycle can save with Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop. Plain concrete gets Foundation Armor SX5000, and stamped concrete gets BEHR Wet-Look. Check local stock and prices online, buy crack filler and primer on the same trip, add a spare pail, and give the job two days: one to prep, one for two thin coats.
